rows.comment: Chart label, says what the chart shows.
Em dash, shouting STEEP, and the 'even though' clause is a hedge. State what the line does.
lineComments: Say strain can fall late in the day when heart rate drops below your waking pace; drop the dash and capitals.
rows.replacement: Effort above your usual waking pace. The line can fall later in the day if your heart rate drops back toward that pace. Built from {drawn} recorded waking minutes.

rows.comment: Correct and needed, but the 'and the two are not comparable' tail is a second claim; split and tighten.
lineComments: Strain sums over recorded minutes, so a partly worn day scores lower. Say not to compare it with a full day.
rows.replacement: Strain adds up the minutes the band recorded, so a partly worn day scores lower than a full one. Don't compare the two.

rows.comment: 'Both measured on you' is a fragment answering nothing; 'we have seen' is vague.
lineComments: Zone edges run between your resting heart rate and your highest recorded heart rate, {maxHr} bpm.
rows.replacement: Zone edges run from your measured resting heart rate to your highest recorded heart rate ({maxHr} bpm).

rows.comment: 'measured, not estimated' rebuts a claim nobody made; em dash.
lineComments: State edges as percentages of the highest recorded rate.
rows.replacement: Zone edges are percentages of your highest recorded heart rate ({maxHr} bpm).

lineComments: Name the content: how strain is calculated.
rows.replacement: How strain is calculated

rows.comment: Banister TRIMP is jargon with no definition; keep the algorithm name and the 0-21 scale, add what it does.
rows.replacement: Banister TRIMP (training impulse, minutes weighted by heart rate) over your waking heart rate, scaled to 0–21.

rows.comment: 'not measured' is a rebuttal and em dash; state source and value.
lineComments: Say it uses an age-and-strap estimate of {maxHr} bpm.
rows.replacement: Strain uses a maximum heart rate of {maxHr} bpm, estimated from your age and strap.

rows.comment: Explains an internal decision with a dramatic reason. State what differs and the consequence.
lineComments: Zone bar uses measured max; strain keeps the estimate so past scores stay unchanged.
rows.replacement: The zone bar above uses your measured maximum. Strain keeps the estimate, so your past scores don't change.

rows.comment: Reasonable mechanism; tighten and name the consequence directly.
lineComments: Resting rate from the previous night is the second input; a missed night shifts the day's score.
rows.replacement: The other input is your resting heart rate from the night before. If the band missed that night, the whole day's strain shifts.
Time by intensity

rows.comment: 'come off your age' is loose; leading space must stay because it is appended to another string.
lineComments: Say zones are calculated from age until a ceiling is measured.
rows.replacement: Until one is measured, the zones below are calculated from your age.

rows.comment: 'A one-second spike is not a heart rate' is an aphorism rebutting nobody. Keep the 15 second rule.
lineComments: State the rule: a reading counts when held 15 seconds while moving.
rows.replacement: A high reading counts only if the band held it for 15 seconds while you were moving.

rows.comment: 'We have seen' is odd; the band recorded it.
lineComments: Label the value as highest recorded.
rows.replacement: HIGHEST RECORDED

rows.comment: Em dash and 'creeps up'; 'Do not go and test it' is a cute safety line. Keep the safety point, say it plainly.
lineComments: It is the highest recorded rate, rises with harder efforts, and is not a target.
rows.replacement: This is the highest heart rate the band has recorded. It rises when you record harder efforts. Don't push to max out to raise it.

rows.comment: Clumsy phrasing; say what to add.
lineComments: Zones need a maximum heart rate, which needs your age.
rows.replacement: Zones are percentages of a maximum heart rate, and the app calculates that from your age. Add your age to get zones.

rows.comment: Em dash and 'not one measured on you' rebuttal.
rows.replacement: Zone edges are percentages of a maximum heart rate estimated from your age.

rows.comment: Awkward; says the cause is unknown.
lineComments: Say the app has no reason recorded.
rows.replacement: The app has no recorded reason for the missing zone edges.

rows.comment: 'These are the usual bands, not your own measured thresholds' rebuts nobody; 'the middle' means median. Keep the facts.
lineComments: Give the two inputs, median resting rate over N nights, and the zone 1 effect; drop the rebuttal.
rows.replacement: Built from your resting rate ({restingHr}, the median of your last {restingDays} nights) and your highest recorded rate ({maxHr}). A low resting rate makes zone 1 wide. The band edges are standard percentages.

rows.comment: 'which fits you better' is vague; rebuttal sentence at the end.
lineComments: State when resting rate is added, with the night counts.
rows.replacement: Built from your highest recorded heart rate ({maxHr}). After {restingMinDays} nights of resting rate (you have {restingDays}), your resting rate is added to the calculation. The band edges are standard percentages.

rows.comment: The 20 bpm error range has no backing located in lib/ (only a credible-gap constant). The Tanaka age formula is cited elsewhere in the code. Keep the number as stated; confirm it against the formula's published standard error.
lineComments: Name the estimate, keep 20 bpm, drop the dash and 'rather than'.
rows.replacement: Built from {maxHr} bpm, estimated from your age with the Tanaka formula. It can be off by 20 bpm either way. The edges switch to a measured maximum once the band records a hard enough session.

rows.comment: 'not computed' antithesis, em dash, and 'whatever' clause.
lineComments: You set these five thresholds; they replace the age or measured values.
rows.replacement: You set these five thresholds. They replace the zones the app would calculate from your age or a measured maximum.

lineComments: Say what to enter and how to reset.
rows.replacement: Enter five bpm thresholds, lowest to highest. Each is where a zone starts. Clear all five to return to the calculated zones.

rows.comment: States the requirement. 'about a month' matches the 28-day chart window.
'a picture of ... not of' is a flourish and rebuttal.
lineComments: Say bars appear once zones use a measured maximum.
rows.replacement: These bars appear once the zone edges above come from a measured maximum. Until then they would only reflect the age estimate.

rows.comment: Trailing ' — a pyramid' is a cute label and em dash.
lineComments: Describe the split and name the pattern.
rows.replacement: Most of your minutes are easy, fewer are in the middle and the fewest are hard (pyramidal).
Most of your minutes are easy and the rest are hard, with little in between (polarised).

rows.comment: 'rather than easy or hard' is an unneeded contrast.
lineComments: Say most minutes are in the middle zones.
rows.replacement: Most of your minutes are in the middle zones.

rows.comment: 'A description, not a target' rebuts nobody.
rows.replacement: {easy} min easy, {moderate} moderate, {hard} hard, over {sessions} recorded sessions.

rows.comment: 'Nothing is uploaded' answers a worry nobody raised, but it is a privacy statement; keep it, state the mechanism, end with a period.
lineComments: Photo is read from the phone and not uploaded.
rows.replacement: The photo is read from this phone and is not uploaded.
Draw the map

rows.comment: Network disclosure must stay; tighten the awkward 'Off,' clause.
lineComments: Say it requests tiles from openstreetmap.org; when off, only the route is drawn.
rows.replacement: Requests the tiles covering this route from openstreetmap.org. When off, only the route is drawn.

rows.comment: 'Everything else ... unchanged' answers an unraised worry.
rows.replacement: The map tiles could not be fetched, so the card shows only the route.

rows.comment: Question prompt for rating; acceptable as a UI prompt.
'which is the point' is flourish; em dash; 'not a measurement' rebuttal.
lineComments: Say it is your rating and may differ from measured numbers.
rows.replacement: Your own rating of the effort. It may differ from the measured numbers above.

rows.comment: Button containing proper noun Strava; label only.
Awkward 'only counts them on foot'; state source and scope.
lineComments: Steps come from the strap's motion sensor and count walking and running only.
rows.replacement: Steps come from the strap's motion sensor, which counts only steps taken on foot.

lineComments: Tell the reader to add weight.
rows.replacement: Add your weight to see calories.

rows.comment: Wordy; split and give the fix.
